1:1.sourceText: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ (Υἱοῦ Θεοῦ).
1:1.targetText: A beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.

review.note: The pinned N1904 places Son of God in parentheses; LSV includes the title. The words are actually present in both displayed witnesses and remain linked.

1:2.sourceText: Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου·
1:2.targetText:
As it has been written in the Prophets: “Behold, I send My messenger before Your face,
Who will prepare Your way before You.

groups.note: N1904 has singular prophet qualifying Isaiah, whereas LSV has plural Prophets. The shared prophetic noun is linked with this number and attribution difference recorded.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Source-witness attribution difference: N1904 names Isaiah, whereas the LSV reading refers to the Prophets collectively; no English Isaiah is present.

unmappedTarget.reason: The additional final before You clause in LSV has no corresponding words in the pinned N1904 verse.

1:3.sourceText: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν Κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ,
1:3.targetText:
A voice of one calling in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the LORD,
Make His paths straight.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:4.sourceText: ἐγένετο Ἰωάνης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.
1:4.targetText: John came immersing in the wilderness, and proclaiming an immersion of conversion for forgiveness of sins,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds a coordinating and before proclaiming; no corresponding conjunction is present in this N1904 verse.

1:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμεῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
1:5.targetText: and there were going forth to him all the region of Judea, and they of Jerusalem, and they were all immersed by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.

groups.note: N1904 places all with the Jerusalem inhabitants; LSV places all in the ensuing immersion clause. The shared quantifier is retained while its English clause placement is acknowledged.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:6.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάνης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
1:6.targetText: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and a girdle of skin around his loins, and eating locusts and honey of the field,

groups.note: Greek wild, qualifying honey, is rendered with the descriptive phrase of the field; no separate Greek field noun is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ.
1:7.targetText: and he proclaimed, saying, “He comes—who is mightier than I—after me, of whom I am not worthy—having stooped down—to loose the strap of His sandals;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies is in who is mightier. Greek has the article and comparative adjective, the mightier one, without a separate being verb in that phrase.

1:8.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ.
1:8.targetText: I indeed immersed you in water, but He will immerse you in the Holy Spirit.”

groups.note: The Greek dative water is rendered with the English preposition in; there is no separate Greek in here.
The dative Spirit phrase is rendered in the Holy Spirit; the English preposition and article express that noun phrase construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English indeed corresponds to no particle in this pinned N1904 verse.

1:9.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάνου.
1:9.targetText: And it came to pass in those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was immersed by John in the Jordan;

groups.note: N1904 has directional εἰς into the Jordan; LSV renders the river relation in. This contextual relation is linked without equating all uses of εἰς and in.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:10.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον εἰς αὐτόν·
1:10.targetText: and immediately coming up from the water, He saw the heavens dividing, and the Spirit coming down on Him as a dove;

groups.note: The Greek directional εἰς is rendered on in the descent upon Him; this is the contextual relation, not an identical preposition form.

1:11.sourceText: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
1:11.targetText: and a voice came out of the heavens, “You are My Son, the Beloved, in whom I delighted.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Source-witness grammatical-person difference: N1904 has σοὶ, in You, addressing Jesus directly; LSV has the relative in whom. Unlike pronoun forms are not linked.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV uses relative whom where the pinned N1904 has second-person σοὶ You; the difference is not hidden by a pronoun identity link.

1:12.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.
1:12.targetText: And immediately the Spirit puts Him forth into the wilderness,

1:13.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
1:13.targetText: and He was there in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan, and He was with the beasts, and the messengers were ministering to Him.

1:14.targetText: And after the delivering up of John, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of the Kingdom of God,

1:15.sourceText: καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces the direct quotation; LSV marks direct speech with punctuation and has no separate that.

1:16.sourceText: Καὶ παράγων παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλεεῖς.
1:16.targetText: And walking by the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon, and his brother Andrew, casting a drag into the sea, for they were fishers,

groups.note: The compound ἀμφιβάλλοντας denotes casting a net around; LSV makes the drag-net object explicit within this single verb rendering.
Greek ἐν with the sea is locative, while LSV describes the casting direction into the sea. The phrase retains the casting location with this directional phrasing noted.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
N1904 explicitly repeats Simon in the brother-of-Simon description; LSV replaces that name with his. Unlike proper-name and pronominal forms are left unpaired.
